name: tag-expression-repeated-same-level
description: A tag is repeated in the same tag group or level.
common_causes: Copy-paste errors creating duplicates
Accidentally adding same tag multiple times
Misunderstanding of tag group equivalency
Redundant expressions in same scope
Not recognizing equivalent tag group orders
explanation: HED treats tag expressions as sets, where order doesn't matter and duplicates are meaningless. Repeated tags or equivalent tag groups at the same level create redundancy and are not allowed.
correction_strategy: Remove duplicate tags and equivalent expressions

correction_examples.explanation: Removed duplicate 'Red' tag
Removed duplicate tag group
Removed equivalent group (order doesn't matter)
Removed the repeated Def tag; unlike identical Definition groups, repeated Def tags are a repeated expression

correction_patterns: Remove identical tags at same level
Remove duplicate tag groups
Remove groups that are equivalent due to order independence
Keep only one instance of repeated expressions
Consider merging related content if appropriate
fix_instructions: 1. Identify repeated tags at the same level
2. Identify equivalent tag groups (same content, different order)
3. Remove duplicates keeping only one instance
4. Verify remaining structure is meaningful
5. Check for nested duplicates at different levels
validation_hints: Compare tags and groups at same nesting level
Remember that tag order within groups doesn't matter
Check for exact duplicates and order-equivalent groups
Verify no repeated expressions remain

name: tags-duplicated-across-multiple-rows
description: Tags are repeated because two rows have the same onset value.
common_causes: Same tag appearing in multiple columns for single event
Tag duplication during sidecar assembly
Overlapping column content creating repeats
Copy-paste errors in event annotations
Unintentional tag repetition across data sources
explanation: When assembling HED annotations from multiple sources (columns, sidecars, direct annotations), the same tag should not appear multiple times in the final annotation for a single event.
correction_strategy: Remove duplicate tags from assembled annotations

correction_examples.wrong: Red (from column 1) + Red (from column 2) = Red, Red
correction_examples.correct: Red (from column 1) + Blue (from column 2) = Red, Blue
correction_examples.explanation: Used different tags or removed duplicate

correction_examples.wrong: Event with Sensory-event in multiple columns
correction_examples.correct: Event with Sensory-event in one column, other content in other columns
correction_examples.explanation: Eliminated duplication across columns

correction_patterns: Check for tag repetition across columns
Remove duplicate tags from one source
Use different but related tags when appropriate
Consolidate related information to avoid duplication
fix_instructions: 1. Identify duplicate tags in assembled annotation
2. Trace back to source columns causing duplication
3. Remove duplicate from one of the sources
4. Verify final assembled annotation has no duplicates
5. Test with multiple rows to ensure consistency
validation_hints: Check final assembled annotations for duplicates
Trace tag sources to identify duplication points
Verify column content doesn't overlap inappropriately
Test annotation assembly across multiple events

name: tags-with-duplicated-onsets-across-multiple-rows
description: Tags are repeated because two rows have the same onset value.
common_causes: Multiple Onset tags for same definition across events
Temporal boundary violations with repeated onsets
Missing Offset tags between repeated Onsets
Incorrect temporal sequence management
Overlapping temporal events without proper boundaries
explanation: Temporal logic requires that Onset tags for the same definition be properly paired with Offset tags. Multiple Onsets without intervening Offsets violate temporal sequencing rules.
correction_strategy: Ensure proper Onset/Offset pairing across events

correction_examples.wrong: Event 1: Onset, Def/Action\nEvent 3: Onset, Def/Action (no Offset between)
correction_examples.correct: Event 1: Onset, Def/Action\nEvent 2: Offset, Def/Action\nEvent 3: Onset, Def/Action
correction_examples.explanation: Added required Offset between repeated Onsets

correction_examples.wrong: Multiple Onsets for same definition without boundaries
correction_examples.correct: Proper Onset/Offset alternation for temporal boundaries
correction_examples.explanation: Maintained temporal logic consistency

correction_patterns: Add missing Offset tags between repeated Onsets
Ensure Onset/Offset alternation for same definitions
Verify temporal boundary consistency across events
Check temporal logic across entire event sequence
fix_instructions: 1. Identify repeated Onset tags for same definition
2. Check for missing Offset tags between them
3. Add required Offset tags to maintain proper sequence
4. Verify temporal logic across all events
5. Test temporal boundary consistency
validation_hints: Onset tags for same definition need Offset between repetitions
Check temporal sequence: Onset → Offset → Onset
Verify temporal logic across entire event sequence
Look for missing temporal boundaries

name: tag-expression-repeated-na-onset-row
description: A tag is repeated in the assembled annotation of a row whose onset is n/a.
common_causes: Repeating in the HED column a tag that the row's sidecar annotation already supplies
Assuming that rows without an onset are not validated
explanation: A row whose onset is n/a is not merged with any other row, but its assembled annotation (the HED column joined with the annotations of its sidecar-annotated columns) is still validated like any other row's. A tag that appears both in the HED column and in the sidecar annotation of the same row is repeated at the top level, wherever the row sits in the file.
correction_strategy: Remove the tag from the HED column or from the sidecar annotation

correction_examples.wrong: event_code show -> "Sensory-event, Visual-presentation" with HED column "Sensory-event, Red"
correction_examples.correct: event_code show -> "Sensory-event, Visual-presentation" with HED column "Red"
correction_examples.explanation: Sensory-event is supplied once, by the sidecar

correction_patterns: Keep each tag in one place: the sidecar or the HED column
Validate rows without an onset the same way as timed rows
fix_instructions: 1. Assemble the annotation of each row whose onset is n/a
2. Find tags that appear in both the HED column and the sidecar annotation
3. Remove one of the two
validation_hints: A row with an n/a onset is validated wherever it appears: first, in the middle, or last
Its assembled annotation is checked for repeats like any other row's

name: tag-expression-repeated-column-name-with-period
description: A curly-brace reference to a column whose name has a period is substituted, and the result repeats a tag.
common_causes: Repeating a tag in a group and in the annotation substituted into it
explanation: A reference such as {my.col} is replaced by the annotation of the my.col column when the row is assembled, whatever characters the column name contains. Here (Red, {my.col}) with my.col value x annotated as Red assembles to (Red, Red), which repeats Red in one group. A validator that does not substitute the reference misses the repeat.
correction_strategy: Remove the tag from the group or from the referenced annotation

correction_examples.explanation: The assembled group (Red, Blue) has no repeat

correction_patterns: Check the assembled annotation, after every curly-brace reference is substituted
fix_instructions: 1. Assemble the row, substituting each referenced column
2. Look for tags repeated within a group
validation_hints: A sidecar in which some value of my.col would repeat a tag fails even for rows with other values; the passing sidecar annotates x as Green

name: tag-expression-repeated-value-case
description: Tags that differ only in the case of a node name, tag extension or definition name are repeated; tags whose values differ in case are not.
common_causes: Writing the same tag twice with different capitalization
Assuming that changing the case of a tag makes it a different tag
Writing a tag extension or definition name twice with different capitalization
Combining a sidecar annotation and a HED column cell that contain the same tag in different case
explanation: Node names, tag extensions and definition names are matched without regard to case, so Red and red, Red/Blech and Red/blech, and Def/MyColor and Def/mycolor are each the same tag expression and may not appear twice at the same level. The value that replaces a # placeholder is matched exactly as written, so Label/abc and Label/ABC are different tag expressions and may both appear.
correction_strategy: Remove one of two tags that differ only in the case of their node names, extensions or definition names. Leave two tags that share a node but whose values differ in case; they are not repeated.

correction_examples.explanation: Node names are matched without regard to case, so red repeats Red
The tag differs only in case and the value is the same, so the expression is repeated
Definition names are matched without regard to case
Tag extensions are matched without regard to case

correction_patterns: Treat tags that differ only in capitalization as the same tag
Keep tags whose values differ, even if only in case
Remove the second of two tags that match without regard to case
fix_instructions: 1. Compare the tags at each level without regard to the case of node names, extensions and definition names
2. Compare values exactly as written
3. Remove one tag of each pair that matches under these rules
4. Leave tags whose values differ only in case
validation_hints: Lowercase node names, extensions and definition names before comparing
Do not change the case of values before comparing
Units are not part of this rule; a unit in the wrong case is UNITS_INVALID

name: tag-expression-repeated-namespace-case
description: Tags that differ only in the case of their namespace prefix are repeated.
common_causes: Writing the same prefixed tag twice with the prefix in different capitalization
Assuming that ts: and TS: are different namespaces
explanation: Namespace names are case-insensitive, so ts:Red and TS:Red are the same tag and may not appear twice at the same level.
correction_strategy: Remove one of two tags that differ only in the case of their namespace prefix.

correction_examples.explanation: ts: and TS: name the same namespace, so TS:Red repeats ts:Red

name: tag-expression-repeated-hed-column-reference
description: A sidecar annotation repeats a tag once its {HED} reference is removed. Under rule 10 of the sidecar curly-brace rules, a {HED} reference is always removed when the sidecar is checked, as it is in a row whose HED cell is n/a or blank, so (Red, {HED}), (Red) is invalid as a sidecar on its own: removing the reference leaves (Red), (Red). The combo item fails on a row whose HED cell is n/a. (Red, {HED}), (Blue) passes.
common_causes: Writing a sidecar annotation that is only valid when the HED column is filled
Repeating in a separate group a tag that sits beside a {HED} reference
explanation: When the HED cell of a row is n/a or blank, the {HED} reference is removed together with its comma, so (Red, {HED}), (Red) assembles to (Red), (Red), which repeats the group (Red). A validator checks every sidecar annotation with the {HED} reference removed, so the sidecar is invalid even if every row of the current file fills the HED column.
correction_strategy: Change the sidecar annotation so it stays valid when the HED column is empty; do not rely on the HED column being filled

correction_examples.explanation: With the reference removed the annotation is (Red), (Blue), which has no repeat
The second (Red) adds nothing; dropping it removes the repeat

correction_patterns: Check each sidecar annotation with every {HED} reference removed
fix_instructions: 1. Find the sidecar annotation that contains {HED}
2. Remove {HED} and its comma, and look for a repeated tag or group
3. Change or remove the repeated tag in the sidecar
validation_hints: The sidecar alone fails; no row is needed to find the error
A row whose HED cell is n/a assembles to the same repeat

name: tag-expression-repeated-reference-removed
description: A sidecar annotation repeats a tag once a curly-brace reference to another column is removed. Under rule 10 of the sidecar curly-brace rules, the annotation is also checked with all its references removed, as in a row whose referenced cell is n/a or blank (rule 3), so (Red, {color}), (Red) is invalid as a sidecar on its own even though no annotation of color is Red, and so is (Red, {rt}), (Red) for a value column rt. The combo items fail on rows whose color cell is n/a or blank (the empty string) and whose rt cell is n/a.
common_causes: Writing a sidecar annotation that is only valid when a referenced column is filled
Repeating in a separate group a tag that sits beside a curly-brace reference
explanation: When a referenced cell is n/a or blank, the reference is removed together with its comma, so (Red, {color}), (Red) assembles to (Red), (Red), which repeats the group (Red). This holds for a categorical column such as color and for a value column such as rt. A validator checks each sidecar annotation with every reference removed, so the sidecar is invalid even if every row of the current file fills the referenced column.
correction_strategy: Change the sidecar annotation so it stays valid when the referenced column is n/a or blank; do not rely on the column being filled

correction_examples.explanation: With the reference removed the annotation is (Red), (Yellow), which has no repeat
The second (Red) adds nothing; dropping it removes the repeat

correction_patterns: Check each sidecar annotation with every curly-brace reference removed
fix_instructions: 1. Find the sidecar annotation with the curly-brace reference
2. Remove each reference and its comma, and look for a repeated tag or group
3. Change or remove the repeated tag in the sidecar
validation_hints: The sidecar alone fails; no row is needed to find the error
A row whose referenced cell is n/a or blank assembles to the same repeat
A blank cell is written as the empty string, so the row keeps as many cells as the header

name: tag-expression-repeated-curly-brace-substitution
description: A sidecar annotation repeats a tag when the annotation of a column it references is substituted. Under rule 10 of the sidecar curly-brace rules, each annotation of each referenced column is substituted, one referenced column at a time with every other reference removed, whether or not a table uses that value. So (Red, {color}) is invalid if an annotation of color is Red, and (Red, {color}), (Blue, {shade}) is invalid for the same color with shade removed. A repeat that needs two referenced columns filled at once, such as ({color}, {shade}) when both give Red, is required only when a row is assembled; the combo fails item pins it, and no sidecar item depends on whether a validator reports it in the sidecar.
common_causes: Annotating a referenced column with a tag the referencing annotation already has
Assuming a sidecar is valid because no row of the current file uses the conflicting value
explanation: A curly-brace reference is replaced by the annotation of the referenced column. If any annotation of that column repeats a tag beside the reference, the substitution has a repeat: (Red, {color}) with color warm annotated Red gives (Red, Red). The sidecar is checked for every annotation of the referenced column, so it is invalid even if no row uses warm.
correction_strategy: Change the referencing annotation or the referenced column's annotation so no substitution repeats a tag; do not rely on rows avoiding the conflicting value

correction_examples.explanation: No annotation of color repeats Red, so every substitution is valid
Substituting color with shade removed gives (Red, Green), (Blue) or (Red, Blue), (Blue), neither of which repeats

correction_patterns: Substitute each annotation of each referenced column, one column at a time, and check the result
fix_instructions: 1. For each annotation with curly braces, list the columns it references
2. For each such column, substitute each of its annotations, removing the other references
3. Look for a repeated tag or group in each result and change the sidecar to remove it
validation_hints: The sidecar fails items fail on the sidecar alone, with no row
A repeat that needs two referenced columns filled is only required at row assembly; a validator MAY also report it in the sidecar
